quiz.title: Module 1 — The Foundations of Communication
quiz.description: Monday's quiz covers the articulation video — surface and deep lexicon — and the foundations of communication: the process, feedback, noise, and the forms communication takes.

questions.prompt: In the video on becoming more articulate, what is the difference between a surface lexicon and a deep lexicon?
options: The surface lexicon contains technical words, while the deep lexicon contains simple words.
The surface lexicon contains words we recognize but rarely use, while the deep lexicon contains words we use daily.
The surface lexicon contains words we naturally default to in everyday speech, while the deep lexicon contains words we recognize but rarely use.
The surface lexicon is written vocabulary, while the deep lexicon is spoken vocabulary.
questions.explanation: Your surface lexicon is what you reach for automatically in everyday speech. Your deep lexicon holds words you know and recognise but do not yet use naturally — which is exactly the gap the Surface Lexicon Exercise works on.

questions.prompt: According to the video, what is one way to help a word move higher in your lexicon and become more natural in your speech?
options: Avoid using the word until you fully understand every possible definition.
Repeat and use the word regularly.
Replace the word with a simpler word whenever possible.
Memorize the word without using it in conversation.
questions.explanation: A word becomes natural through use, not memorisation. Repeating and using it is what moves it from recognition into your everyday speech.

questions.prompt: What does the video recommend doing before speaking when you want to find a more precise word?
options: Speak immediately so you do not lose your thought.
Use filler words while searching for an answer.
Give yourself a little more time to search your vocabulary.
Repeat the first word that comes to mind.
questions.explanation: Precision takes a moment. Allowing yourself a brief pause to search your vocabulary is how you find the right word instead of settling for the first one.

questions.prompt: In the communication process, which sequence best represents the basic flow described in the lesson?
options: Receiver → Message → Sender → Feedback → Medium
Sender → Message → Medium → Receiver → Feedback
Message → Sender → Receiver → Medium → Feedback
Sender → Receiver → Message → Medium → Context
questions.explanation: The sender creates a message, sends it through a medium, the receiver interprets it, and feedback returns to the sender — all of it shaped by context.

questions.prompt: Why is feedback important in the communication process?
options: It allows the sender to know how the receiver responded to or understood the message.
It prevents the sender from choosing a communication medium.
It guarantees that communication will never be misunderstood.
It replaces the need for a message.
questions.explanation: Feedback is how the sender finds out whether the meaning they intended is the meaning that arrived. Without it, you are guessing.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of communication noise?
options: Choosing a clear communication channel
Giving someone feedback
A distracted listener misunderstanding an important message
Organizing a message before sending it
questions.explanation: Noise is anything that interferes with the message before it is understood — including a distracted listener, not just physical sound.

questions.prompt: According to the video on types of communication, which form of communication primarily uses facial expressions, gestures, eye contact, posture, and body movement?
options: Written communication
Visual communication
Verbal communication
Non-verbal communication
questions.explanation: Non-verbal communication is everything sent without relying primarily on spoken words — expressions, gestures, posture, eye contact and body movement.

questions.prompt: A company creates an infographic containing charts, images, colours, and symbols to explain complicated information to its audience. Which type of communication is being used most directly?
options: Visual communication
Verbal communication
Written communication
Non-verbal communication
questions.explanation: Charts, images, colours and symbols communicate meaning through visual elements, which is visual communication.
